method: All inputs are read in the browser and nothing is sent anywhere. Shade depth is the mass of dye powder as a percentage of the dry fabric mass (% WOF), so dye grams = fabric grams x depth / 100. The bath ratio is litres of water per kilogram of fabric, so water litres = fabric grams x ratio / 1000, and dye per litre follows from the two. Fabric can be entered directly, or as length x width x gsm (grams per square metre) which is the fabric mass per unit area. Accepted ranges: 1 to 20,000 g of fabric, sides 1 to 2,000 cm, 10 to 2,000 g/m2, shade depth 0.01 to 20 %, bath ratio 1 to 50 litres per kilogram. The calculator only does this arithmetic: powder strength varies by dye class, and salt, soda ash, temperature, time and pH come from the dye maker's recipe. The grams assume the stated shade depth is fully taken up, and no safety, disposal or fabric-compatibility guidance is implied.

sources.title: Dyeing - recipes are commonly expressed as a percentage of the dry mass of the fibre, the weight of fibre (WOF)
Units of textile measurement - grams per square metre (gsm) gives the mass of a fabric per unit area
